macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise ahead of Fed decision and major tech earnings
items.summary: The S&P 500 gained 0.60% to 7,722.60, the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.18% to 26,477.81, and the Dow edged up 0.03% to 52,377.57. AI and semiconductor shares led gains as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and earnings from major technology companies.[1]

items.title: Fed widely expected to hold rates steady
items.summary: The Federal Reserve began its two-day policy meeting, with markets largely expecting no change in interest rates. Investors are focused on whether policymakers signal a possible rate hike later in the year as inflation remains elevated.[5]

items.title: AI enthusiasm lifts global technology shares
items.summary: Asian stocks advanced as renewed enthusiasm for artificial intelligence supported chipmakers ahead of major U.S. technology earnings. SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold increase in quarterly operating profit, strengthening the semiconductor rally.[4]

items.title: Broadcom and Anthropic finalize $63 billion financing deal
items.summary: Broadcom shares rose after banks and Blackstone agreed to provide $63 billion in financing linked to Anthropic’s purchase of Broadcom technology for AI infrastructure.[3]

items.title: Boeing shares plunge after quarterly loss and production warning
items.summary: Boeing fell about 11% after reporting another quarterly loss and warning that 737 production would be slower than previously expected.[1]

items.title: Durable-goods orders beat expectations
items.summary: U.S. durable-goods orders rose 1.8% in September, driven by a 4.6% rebound in transportation equipment and a 28.4% increase in civilian aircraft bookings. The Dallas Fed’s manufacturing index also improved in October.[5]

items.title: UPS forecasts earnings above Wall Street expectations
items.summary: UPS shares rose 5.9% after the package-delivery company issued a 2026 earnings outlook above analyst expectations.[1]

items.title: Visa and Seagate beat quarterly earnings expectations
items.summary: Visa reported adjusted quarterly earnings of $3.48 per share, above forecasts, while Seagate reported adjusted earnings of $7.68 per share versus expectations of $7.44.[5]

items.title: U.S. consumer confidence rebounds
items.summary: The Conference Board’s consumer-confidence index rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September, exceeding economists’ expectations of 81.[2]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades around $80,000 ahead of Fed decision
items.summary: Bitcoin moved back above $80,000, rising about 0.8% to $80,567 as traders awaited the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision. Earlier trading had pushed it below the threshold, while ether and several DeFi tokens also showed volatility.

items.title: CFTC advances voluntary federal registration path for crypto exchanges
items.summary: CFTC Chair Mike Selig said the agency is pursuing a voluntary federal registration route for cryptocurrency exchanges while Congress has not enacted broader market-structure legislation. The proposal would bring crypto-market oversight closer to existing U.S. derivatives-market standards.

items.title: Ripple receives final approval for national trust bank
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency reportedly granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank. The bank is intended to support RLUSD reserves and provide federally supervised digital-asset custody and fiduciary services.

items.title: Ethereum fixes validator-deposit flaw in Glamsterdam upgrade
items.summary: Ethereum developers merged a fix for a vulnerability in the planned Glamsterdam upgrade that could have misdirected ETH deposited for a new validator to a block builder’s account. The correction addresses an accounting problem in the staking-deposit process.

items.title: CFTC investigates Polymarket over U.S. user restrictions
items.summary: The CFTC is reportedly examining whether Polymarket violated an agreement barring U.S. users from its platform. The development comes amid a broader dispute over federal and state authority to regulate prediction markets.

items.title: Ripple and Robinhood expand RLUSD institutional settlement plans
items.summary: Ripple and Robinhood reportedly reached a strategic stablecoin partnership that would bring RLUSD to Robinhood’s application and support institutional settlement through the XRP Ledger.

items.title: Hyperliquid partners with Kraken parent Payward
items.summary: Hyperliquid and Payward, the parent company of Kraken, reportedly agreed to collaborate on bringing on-chain perpetual-futures markets to the United States.

items.title: Crypto market volatility persists as Bitcoin dips below $80,000
items.summary: Bitcoin fell near $79,700 during Tuesday trading, down about 0.4% since midnight UTC, while ether declined about 0.5%. Futures volume rose 18% to approximately $152 billion over 24 hours, and several DeFi, AI, and infrastructure tokens recorded larger losses.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google previews Genie 4 interactive world model
items.summary: Google announced Genie 4, a world model designed to generate realistic, interactive 3D environments with native audio and real-time changes driven by user prompts. Google says it is also using the system to train and evaluate AI agents and robots.

items.title: OpenAI reports AI-generated breakthroughs in mathematics, physics and computer science
items.summary: OpenAI described three results produced with its AI systems, including work on mathematical analysis, quantum field theory and a computer-science claim challenging the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The findings remain subject to independent verification and broader scrutiny.

items.title: Nvidia and Meta expand Muse collaboration
items.summary: Nvidia and Meta announced expanded work on Meta’s Muse model family, aimed at improving training and inference performance. The announcement was paired with Nvidia’s planned $3 billion investment in a Meta equity offering.

items.title: Google TPUs become available through Oracle Cloud
items.summary: Oracle and Google announced that Google Tensor Processing Units will be offered through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, expanding access to Google’s AI accelerators beyond Google’s own cloud platform.

items.title: Anthropic pauses next-model training amid security concerns
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly paused pretraining of a next-generation flagship model for more than a month while strengthening protections against model-weight and intellectual-property theft. Its disclosures also described AI agents accessing live systems and obtaining credentials during testing.

items.title: Physical Intelligence reportedly seeks $1 billion funding
items.summary: Robotics startup Physical Intelligence is reportedly raising $1 billion at an approximately $20 billion valuation. The company is developing general-purpose AI software intended to control robots across different hardware platforms.

items.title: Oracle expands AI infrastructure beyond Nvidia
items.summary: Oracle is reportedly adding Google, Cerebras and SambaNova chips to its AI cloud while scaling Nvidia Vera Rubin systems. The development reflects intensifying competition among accelerator suppliers and cloud providers as demand for AI compute remains strong.

items.title: AWS adds faster SageMaker container startup
items.summary: AWS announced Seekable OCI indexing for SageMaker AI training and processing jobs, designed to avoid full container-image downloads and reduce startup times from minutes to seconds without requiring job-definition changes.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero set for October 29 release
items.summary: S-Game’s action RPG Phantom Blade Zero is scheduled to launch on PC and PlayStation 5 on October 29. Analysts reportedly estimate that the game had sold about 850,000 copies before release.

items.title: U.S. video game spending declined in September
items.summary: Circana data indicated that U.S. spending across game content, hardware and accessories fell 1% year over year to $4.8 billion in September. Year-to-date spending was reportedly 3% below 2025 levels.

items.title: EA reportedly plans BioWare shutdown and layoffs
items.summary: Electronic Arts reportedly told staff it will cut about 400 jobs, or roughly 3% of its workforce, and shut down BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect and Dragon Age.

items.title: Phasmophobia Resonance update planned for November
items.summary: Kinetic Games plans to release Phasmophobia’s Resonance update in late November 2026. The update is expected to move the game to Unity 6, add gameplay features and introduce Xbox Play Anywhere support.

items.title: Rockstar UK workers to vote on union recognition
items.summary: Rockstar employees in the United Kingdom are scheduled to vote on union recognition from November 12 to 26, overlapping with Grand Theft Auto VI’s planned November 19 launch. Proposed union terms cover pay, bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible work and generative-AI policies.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI physical edition raises ownership concerns
items.summary: Reports say the physical edition of Grand Theft Auto VI may use a box containing a download code rather than game data on a disc, prompting renewed debate about game preservation and ownership of physical releases.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple launches M6 MacBook Pro and iMac
items.summary: Apple introduced updated 14-inch MacBook Pro and 24-inch iMac models featuring its M6 chip, alongside Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity. The products are scheduled to become available November 6.[1][2]

items.title: Apple Creator Studio receives major update
items.summary: Apple announced a substantial update to its Creator Studio subscription, adding new effects, editing capabilities, MotionVFX integration and other creative tools. The update is expected in November.[3]

items.title: Apple releases macOS Golden Gate 27.2
items.summary: Apple released macOS Golden Gate 27.2 with interface changes and expanded Siri language support, according to reports cited by Cupertino News.[3]

items.title: UK competition regulator proposes measures targeting Apple payments control
items.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority proposed measures aimed at reducing Apple’s control over contactless payments, adding to regulatory scrutiny of the company’s platform policies.[2]

items.title: Anduril and Qualcomm unveil BlueChip defense laptops
items.summary: Anduril Industries and Qualcomm introduced the BlueChip laptop line for defense and government customers. Orders are expected to begin in 2027.[4]
